summary.headline: Sasken Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹339 Cr, with software services margin up 240 bps to 30.6% while Product Solutions margin fell to 5.9%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 24% YoY and 1.6% QoQ to ₹339 Cr, led by Software Services at ₹219 Cr (+24.3% YoY). Product Solutions revenue was ₹120 Cr (+23.6% YoY, -3.9% QoQ) after a strong Q4, with memory availability and component pricing pressure. Gross margin was 21.9% (₹74 Cr), and EBIT margin was 6.3%, while PAT was ₹23 Cr (6.9% margin) and was hit by normalisation of Q4 other-income one-offs. Order booking was US$47 million TCV, including US$34 million of new deal wins, with five new logos added.

financial_highlights.change: -310 bps QoQ (Keshav Sureka cited 12.8% prior period)
Sequential decline from Q4 one-off other income and lower FX gains

segments.name: Software Services
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹219 Cr, up 24.3% YoY and 4.8% QoQ; gross margin expanded 240 bps to 30.6% on utilisation, cost discipline and scale. Management says the segment grew more than 20% YoY.

segments.name: Product Solutions (incl. Borqs)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹120 Cr, up 23.6% YoY but down 3.9% QoQ; gross margin fell to 5.9% from 9.0% in Q4 (per the 310 bps decline) due to memory cost pass-through, lower incremental margin and silicon productization mix. Management expects margins to stabilise over the full year.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin guidance; management said it will maintain margins while growing, using efficiency and value pricing.
Management targets US$4 million run-rate revenue for 93 active customers under its 60x4x3 strategy; timeline may stretch by one or two years beyond three.
Breakeven for Borqs at about US$12 million quarterly revenue, per CFO.
Expect large cash consumption in FY27 from working capital and fixed assets; management is working toward cash-flow positive, using internal accruals and external funds.
capex_capacity: Inaugurated Sasken Silicon Incubation Center in Hubballi to build semiconductor talent.
Opened a new centre of excellence in Hyderabad.
Inventory build in Q1 to manage memory shortage contributed to negative cash flow; some silicon products ship through the year.
Silicon business is shifting toward productization; capacity expansion requires working capital.
demand_pricing: Order booking US$47 million TCV (US$34 million new), ACV about US$40 million (US$24 million new); the TCV is not total backlog, and management targets a 9–10 month revenue carry.
Five new logos; 93 active customers vs 79 a year ago; top-five customer share ~56% (vs ~52% previously).
Two hyperscaler engagements (different hyperscalers): a multi-year capability engagement and an OS sustenance engagement, plus an AI and automation deal covering agentic AI and LLM validation.
CSAT 4.5 out of 5 vs industry benchmark 3.75.
Revenue mix: North America 30%, EMEA ~25%, India 26%, APAC ~20%.
Automotive: Borqs instrument cluster module ready but Chinese-sourced modules remain price-competitive; no commercial order yet.
Memory pricing and component costs are being passed through to customers, but incremental margin is not recovered.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, customer wins and Software Services margins, but cautious and non-committal on Product Solutions margins and cash flow. Management declined to give margin guidance, disclosed no project-level detail, and deferred on specific partnership and order-level questions.
key_quotes: We will make sure that we will maintain our margins while we maintain our growth momentum.
So, we do not want to give any guidance on the margins at this point in time, but as Rajiv mentioned, right, so we are constantly making sure that we are driving efficiencies in how we are doing.
So, it is a function of how the customer does the offtake of some of these products.
